svg.text: Everything that was hand-wired on the Pi Proto Board, plus the Qwiic / STEMMA QT cable chain.
1 · I²C and power: Qwiic / STEMMA QT cables (3.3 V)
4 cm: NeoKey right socket → Rotary right socket
The ADS1115 gets power and I²C only via its STEMMA QT sockets; the proto board does not plug into GPIO.
2 · Analogue inputs: one voltage divider per channel (on the Pi Proto Board)
V(An) = 3.3 V × R_trimmer / (R_sensor + R_trimmer): the reading rises as the sensor resistance drops and falls as it rises. Set each trimmer near the sensor's resting resistance for the widest swing.
A+ and A− are supply OUTPUTS of the Adafruit ADS1115 breakout (3.3 V through a ferrite). Do not connect them to the Pi's 3.3 V / 5 V pins.
Sensor: a piezoresistive textile stretch or pressure sensor wired between the TIP and SLEEVE of a 3.5 mm plug (upper leg of the divider).
Each trimmer is used as a variable resistor (wiper tied to one end) and is the lower leg. Jack: tip = A+, sleeve = signal, ring not connected.
* Optional 1 kΩ resistor in series with each trimmer: not part of the original protoboard build (use a wire link to reproduce it exactly), but recommended. It limits the current
if a trimmer is turned all the way down while the sensor is pressed hard, which would otherwise short A+ to A−. It will be included on the upcoming custom PCB replacing the protoboard.
